plugins.name: task
plugins.description: Markdown task management: task files with an embedded workflow table that is the state, epics whose sub-tasks join by their epic: field (worked or finished whole by name or id) and an O(1) epic index, atomic lock-guarded ID allocation safe across parallel sessions, and optional tags (filter, group, reused by Claude, new ones only with your OK, a cheap backlog review to apply one), and scripted listing — filters, grouping, a one-block-per-task digest, epic views with closed work collapsed. Runtime-free (bash + awk); storage location is per-project, and a linked git worktree resolves to the main tree's tasks.

plugins.name: session-storage
plugins.description: Session-scoped key-value storage for Claude Code. Store and retrieve data tied to individual sessions with automatic cleanup.

plugins.name: docs-manager
plugins.description: Treat docs as a product: auto-generated _index.md navigation, broken-link checks, text-source diagrams with typed refs and staleness tracking, a how-to for drawing ERDs that hold up, a method for keeping an agent instruction file (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md) small by moving project knowledge into the docs, cards that catalogue external reference files (pdf, docx, xlsx) with where-to-look maps, runtime-free docx/xlsx extraction, staleness checks that name the docs to review, onboarding of a legacy project (survey its scattered docs, approve a plan, build docs/ with git history and links kept), and the docs-as-product conventions, DRY and SOLID read for docs. No renderer, no runtime, no dependencies.

plugins.name: task-roadmap
plugins.description: Abstract-Gantt roadmap for a markdown task set: scheduled by dependencies and estimates, grouped by epic, critical path highlighted; self-contained HTML, auto-regenerated on task changes; from a git worktree it charts the main tree's tasks.

plugins.name: delay
plugins.description: Delay long-running jobs, such as slow autotest suites, to the user's run window on a Mac: Claude queues a .sh script with params for the project's docker container (a duplicate is a no-op) and reminds the user to start the runner; the user approves the container + script pair once with sudo (sha256-pinned, red-flag checked, including scripts that run a param as a command); the user's sudo start.sh schedules a pmset wake and loads the runner, which runs the jobs with the screen locked, keeps the results, and unloads itself (no always-on daemon). Runtime-free (bash + awk); macOS + launchd.

plugins.name: crew
plugins.description: Run several Claude Code sessions on one working tree and one branch without lost edits: a coordinator/worker playbook (one task, one session: `crew task` records each session's task, refuses one another session owns and hands it over with --take, and status shows who is on what; to work on a task in parallel, split it into sub-tasks), opt-in membership (a session outside the crew works as usual), identity by display name, unique across crews on one machine, a one-screen status of every dirty path by owner, crew-tagged hand-off messages with a durable mailbox (inbox, unread notices, a Stop check), hot-spot holds, a silence watchdog that wakes the coordinator, a slot queue for machine time (cpu / exclusive / quiet) shared by every crew on the machine, copies (detached worktrees in .worktrees/) landed with a merge-or-refuse apply, a worktree per task when the user chooses it for the project or one task (branch task/<ID>, synced by merge or rebase, merged back by the coordinator, its own git guards), local files linked into a new worktree and the setup step printed, a read-only Docker compose report, a snapshot before every edit, exact-path-list commits, no commit or push unless the user says so for the project (asked once), and guard hooks that deny whole-index git commands. `crew end` disbands a crew and gives the repo back its no-crew state, `crew active` tells scripts whether a crew runs, and crew-only project rules (crewRules) are shown to members only. Layered project/user config; costs nothing in repos without a crew. A bare `crew` command on PATH. Runtime-free (bash + awk + git).

plugins.name: kickoff
plugins.description: Kick off a new project with one standard questionnaire that collects what is known and makes the starting decisions with you. It is generic: it names no language, stack, vendor or tool — those come from the answers, and Claude proposes the options that depend on them. Questions branch on earlier answers and are asked in dependency order, each with pre-defined options (at most four) and a default; questions about the sibling plugins (crew, task, task-roadmap) are asked only when they are installed. A quality level (None, Basic, Standard, Full) decides the generic checks per aspect, and each aspect then asks only what to drop or add. Answers are recorded in the project; a charter (overview, goal, scope, numbered decisions with their reasons, open questions) and a quality doc are generated from them. Questions with a real trade-off — the quality level, when backward compatibility starts to apply — are always asked explicitly. It then sets the project up: a small instructions-only CLAUDE.md, and the task config with a workflow carrying the practices you keep (INVEST, tests first, SOLID, DRY), in the repo or outside it for a client project. A machine-wide dev-port registry hands each project a free port, and your own defaults, kept per Claude account, override the questionnaire's. On an existing project it proposes answers from what the project already holds — its files, README, docs and code — each with evidence, marks them recovered in the charter, then closes the gaps between the answers and the code (each one done now, made a task, or left by your choice); edited files are shown as a diff instead of overwritten. Runtime-free (bash + awk).
